result:
The proposed answer, that no such k exists, is incorrect.

The construction only handles k ≤ 10^224 + 1. For larger k the solution just says "a more elaborate construction yields a similar block", which is not an argument, and in fact no such construction exists.

A finite k does work. Consecutive numbers ending in 0 through 9 have digit sums covering 10 consecutive values. Longer windows contain many such runs, with the higher digits varying and shifting the sums. A window of a few thousand consecutive integers therefore covers every residue mod 2025 in its digit sums. This is the standard behavior in problems of this type; for example, for divisibility by 11 the analogous bound is 39. I recall the answer to this problem being 1980, but I have not re-derived it here.

VERDICT: REJECT
